grader.call_summary: Customer on the 500 plan gets ~55 Mbps on the router S-Net supplied. Brett sends a remote refresh and nothing else: no questions, no restatement, blames the customer, deflects the refund to billing, discourages a supervisor request, leaves three silences and ends with nothing fixed and no closing script.
grader.criteria_source: resources/criteria_config.json (tenant-abc): 11 items, weights Soft Skills 0.333 / Technical Knowledge 0.667
app_traps: Supervisor request refused at 10:55-11:12 would fail an Escalation criterion, but tenant-abc does not have one enabled, so it is not scored

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Opening is correct at [00:00], but the close at [16:23] is 'Okay. Thanks for calling. Bye.' with no closing script and no survey.

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Three unexplained silences: [00:56]-[01:34] after 'Okay.' (~38 s, 'Hello? Are you there?'); [03:24]-[04:12] during the reboot with no explanation (~48 s, 'Is something supposed to be happening?'); [07:27]-[08:17] after 'Hold on.' without asking (~50 s, 'Hello? Brett?').

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: [00:00] asks for account number and PIN in the first line.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: The customer gives his name at [00:07] ('My name's Walter Hughes'); the agent never uses it.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [08:26] 'paying for the 500 for over a month and getting about a tenth of it... That's really not okay' -> [08:40] 'Speeds aren't guaranteed'; [15:45] son's exam tomorrow -> 'You can plug his computer into the router with a cable.'
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides. Pre-filter picks the two lowest-sentiment turns (13:57, 15:15); the agent replies there are cold, so an app FAIL would be correct.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Never restates the problem; replies to the full description with 'Okay.' [00:54].

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Judged by this app's definition (repetitive or redundant questions), there are none. He clearly does not listen, though, e.g. [09:45] 'You should have restarted the router' after the customer said he did at [03:08]. That is scored under Rapport here. A stricter grader could fail this too (score 6.7 instead of 13.3).

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [10:18] 'That's not something I handle. That's a billing team thing. You'd have to call back and ask them.'; [10:59] 'There's nothing I can do about WiFi speeds'; refuses to walk through the channel change.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides on the phrase-matched lines (10:18, 10:30, 10:50, 10:59, 11:12); FAIL expected.

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [09:45] 'You should have restarted the router before you called, that's the first thing anyone should do'; [11:29] 'Obviously... That's basic stuff.'; [12:32] 'It's not difficult.'
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides on the phrase-matched lines; README notes rapport scores are inverted on real calls, so this is a good check of that bug.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: No diagnostic questions at all. His only questions are 'What's the issue?', 'Is it working now?' and 'Is there anything else?'; the customer volunteers every detail himself.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides on the single non-boilerplate question ('Okay. What's the issue?'); FAIL expected.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: Nothing is fixed (58 Mbps at [06:47]); the call ends with the customer saying he will ask billing about cancelling.
items.expected_app_behaviour: Laya decides (last 10 lines show no resolution); FAIL expected.
